summary: Construct the local Langlands map for the split exceptional group G₂ over characteristic-zero nonarchimedean fields through exceptional theta lifting, classical packets, triality and spin-valued Galois representations. Determine its enhanced fibres and analytic characterizations, and build the weak PGSp₆ correspondence from standard and spin transfers. Keep the cubic selfdual packets, the induced Siegel spin comparison and the omitted proper-Levi cases explicit, with the exact residual-characteristic and globalization hypotheses. This is a complete target-level planning pass, not a proof-closed or implemented correspondence.

nodes.title: Exceptional dual-group embeddings

nodes.title: Quadratic twist rigidity on the G₂ image
nodes.statement: Let ρ:Γ→G₂(ℂ) be completely reducible and χ:Γ→{±1} nontrivial. If iρ and χ·iρ are not Spin₇-conjugate, then (vρ)⊗χ has no invariant vector. In particular, if s(χ·iρ)≅1⊕vρ, then χ·iρ is conjugate to iρ.
hypotheses: Γ is a group, ρ is completely reducible, and χ is a nontrivial quadratic character.
proofSteps: Apply HKT Lemma 4.6 to the semisimple Zariski closure. A trivial summand in the twisted spin representation gives an invariant nonisotropic spinor after choosing a nondegenerate fixed subspace.
Its stabilizer is G₂; invoke standard injectivity. Do not use the false assertion that every nonzero isotropic spinor has stabilizer G₂.
acceptance: A χ-stable exceptional image may have a nontrivial quadratic stabilizer; the conclusion is conjugacy, not χ=1.

sources.match: Lemma 4.6 gives the contrapositive twist-rigidity criterion for a completely reducible G₂ image. The proof here makes the invariant spinor nonisotropic using semisimplicity.

nodes.title: Weak equivalence and elementwise conjugacy
nodes.statement: Two admissible Spin₇(ℂ) parameters are weakly equivalent exactly when their values at every element of W_F×SL₂(ℂ) are Spin₇-conjugate. This relation can be strictly weaker than conjugacy by a single element.
hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero; p is its residue characteristic.

Recover the standard and spin representation isomorphisms from characters on a reductive Zariski closure. For the forward implication at every W_F×SL₂ element, additionally prove that conjugacy of semisimple parts extends to the commuting unipotent parts; neither a compact maximal subgroup nor Zariski density alone supplies conjugacy on nonsemisimple elements.

nodes.title: The spectrum detected by a quaternion period
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, O a totally definite octonion k-algebra split at every finite place, G=Aut(O), and D⊂O a quaternion subalgebra. Let G_D fix D pointwise. Inside L²(G(k)\G(A_k)), L²_D is the orthogonal complement of the closed span of automorphic representations all of whose vectors have zero G_D(k)\G_D(A_k)-period. The period uses the fixed quotient measure.
hypotheses: k,O,G,D as in the statement; periods are defined on automorphic smooth vectors.
proofSteps: Import automorphic Hilbert spaces and homogeneous-space measures.
Take the closed zero-period spectral span before taking its orthogonal complement; do not define a pointwise kernel of an unbounded period functional on arbitrary L² vectors.
acceptance: Every irreducible automorphic copy contained in L²_D has a nonzero period. A copy with zero period has zero projection. Nonzero period on an arbitrary embedded copy does not by itself imply containment in L²_D when multiplicities occur.

sources.match: The selected space is the orthogonal complement of all zero-period spectral copies. The source deduces nonvanishing on copies contained in it, without an iff for arbitrary embedded copies.

nodes.title: Shin’s automorphic density input
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, G connected reductive with discrete series at infinity, and A_G×ℝ=A_{G,ℝ}. Let S be finite, G unramified away from S and infinity, and Z(G)=1. For a relatively quasi-compact Plancherel-regular subset U of the local unitary dual at S with positive Plancherel measure, infinitely many cuspidal automorphic representations have S-component in U, are unramified outside S and infinity, and are discrete series at infinity. The theorem itself does not prescribe arbitrary spin-regular archimedean parameters.

In the usual C₃ dominant-weight coordinates take λ_t=t(8,4,2), t∈ℕ_{>0}, at every real place. Its coordinate sum 14t is even, so it belongs to the PGSp₆ root lattice. With ρ=(3,2,1), put h=λ_t+ρ=(8t+3,4t+2,2t+1). The inequalities h₁>h₂+h₃ and h₂>h₃>0 make the eight half-signed sums (±h₁±h₂±h₃)/2 distinct: in any signed difference the largest nonzero coordinate dominates all smaller ones. All positive-root pairings tend to infinity, as required by Definition 3.5. A common central normalization shift does not alter distinctness.
